_help: Persistent user feedback log. Each entry maps to a piece. Run scripts/sync_taste.py to push unsynced entries into taste.json iterate_when_chosen (the mutation queue). After mutation runs, iterate_when_chosen is cleared — but this log is permanent.

entries.text: Narrative arc (TOGETHER→LOSS→SEEKING→RETURN) works. But the dawn-sky vertical gradient backdrop is too LOUD/BLANK and reads as empty canvas first. DIAL DOWN the gradient saturation and add subtle texture: starfield specks, low ground horizon, atmospheric scatter, or paper grain. The world should feel inhabited, not like a default sky-blue background.

STRONGER COLOR REIN-IN than the earlier note (which already said -25-40% lightness, -30% saturation). User repeated 2026-05-07: 'oversaturated, fix that.' Pull the palette FURTHER: max saturation 35% on any color, max lightness 65%, prefer earth tones / dusk / smoky tones / patina. NO neon, no vibrant primaries. If a color reads as 'pop' or 'vibrant', it's too saturated — desaturate again. Plus motion still halved (LERP α 0.05→0.02). Restraint is the goal.

Current motion doesn't read coherently — particles move without intention. FIX: replace whatever motion exists with ONE clearly-readable physical or narrative law. Pick one: gravity (everything falls), wind from one direction (unidirectional drift), tidal in-out (radial breathing), spiral attractor pull, or a directed signal-propagation (impulse from one point spreading). Whichever is chosen, the viewer must be able to NAME the law in 5 seconds. No more 'general agitation.'

Two changes: (1) STRAIGHT LINES ONLY — replace any curves with straight line segments (THREE.LineSegments / Line2). (2) NO SUDDEN MOVEMENT — all transitions LERP smoothly with α≤0.04, velocity capped, no jumps or snaps. Steer the OVERALL FEELING toward JOY — warm palette (gold, pink, sunset coral, cream — never cold or muted), rising or upward-flowing motion (gravity-defying), gentle bouncing at endpoints, lightness in the rig. Think: confetti settling, sunrise rays, children's drawings, a balloon's slow ascent.

Expand from a single audio-particle field into MEANINGFULLY-COMPOSED CURLY-LEAVES WORLD. Build 5-12 distinct curly-leaf elements at varying scale (some intimate close-up, some distant), each leaf rendered as a SHEET (ParametricGeometry / curved Plane with bezier midrib), with calligraphic edge curl. ARRANGE them as if composing a small terrarium / a garden vignette / a coral grove / a library of unfurling pages. Add depth-stratification so closer leaves are larger + warmer-lit, distant leaves smaller + cooler. The audio reactivity drives subtle leaf-edge breathing, NOT general jitter. World-feel: someone has CURATED these leaves; they belong together. MOTION-VARIETY HARD RULE (user 2026-05-07): pieces like td1 currently OVER-USE rotation. Iterations of td1 must use a NON-ROTATIONAL motion law from the 10-word vocabulary in scripts/motion_graph.json — pick from drift / pulse / cascade / murmur / ascend / shatter / trace / breathe / propagate. Pure rotation (or 'spinning around an axis') is BANNED for td1 descendants until other motion words have been explored.

lk6 is interesting — keep the structural form. (1) MAKE COLOR INTENTFUL — currently the palette feels random; pick 2-3 colors with a stated reason (e.g. 'oxide red + bone white + amber accent because the form evokes a kiln-fired ceramic'), and apply them with HIERARCHY (one dominant 70%, one supporting 25%, one accent 5%). Each color must serve the form, not decorate it. State the palette reason in a comment at the top of the HTML.

Same aesthetic problem as [[a2p]]: movement is interesting, greyness is not great. Apply the same gray-box fix: any opaque flat gray panel → translucent lustrous surface (frosted glass register: opacity 0.12–0.22, thin inner-edge highlight, faint additive specular shimmer, very slight warm tint). Additionally, this is audio-reactive (FFT, 5 bands) — the movement should feel more directly driven by audio: each frequency band should visibly modulate a DISTINCT visual parameter (e.g. sub-bass → global scale pulse, mid → color saturation shift, high → particle emission burst). Currently movement may be interesting but the audio connection may not be legible. Make the audio causality OBVIOUS — viewer should be able to point at what frequency is doing what.

KEEP the movement — it's interesting. FIX the gray box: replace any opaque/flat gray panel or background rect with a translucent lustrous surface. Target look: frosted glass or polished resin — semi-transparent (opacity 0.12–0.22), with a subtle inner-edge highlight (thin 1px stroke at rgba(255,255,255,0.18)), a faint specular shimmer (additive blending on a plane slightly in front, opacity 0.06–0.1), and a very slight warm tint (rgba(220,200,170,0.08) over the gray base). The box should feel like it belongs to the world — not a UI chrome element overlaid on top. If the gray box is a label/HUD, consider moving it to a minimal monospace overlay at the edge of the canvas instead.

STEER TOWARD FUTURE CITY GRID — both um5 and its parent 5i1 are L-system organic, but um5 should diverge hard into urban structure. Concrete vision: an infinite isometric city grid viewed from above (or a slight tilt), rendered as glowing street-lines on a dark ground plane; buildings as extruded rectangular prisms with lit windows (InstancedMesh + emissive material); L-system rules govern BLOCK SUBDIVISION not branch growth — each iteration splits a block into smaller parcels, recursively, like a generative Mondrian urbanism. Palette: deep navy / charcoal ground + amber/cyan window glow + occasional magenta accent tower. Motion: slow camera drift that reveals the city as it generates outward from a central seed block. Atmosphere: light bloom on tall towers, fog falloff at city horizon. Goal: viewer should immediately read 'future city' — not abstract geometry.

BREAK THE FORM — the current attractor+glyph execution is conceptually right but visually expected. Pick ONE of these unexpected structural moves and commit to it fully: (A) DUAL-ATTRACTOR CIVIL WAR — at t≈20s, a second attractor (Thomas symmetric or Halvorsen) phase-locks with the Aizawa; particles are caught between two gravitational bodies, forming visible bifurcation threads and contested zones where glyphs flicker between two alphabets (Latin vs CJK / Arabic); the two attractors slowly drift apart then re-merge — metaphor: language vs code fighting for the same minds. Implement as two GPGPU ping-pong textures blended by a per-particle ownership scalar. (B) CURSOR WRITES THE POEM — pointer doesn't nudge parameters, it ABSORBS nearby glyphs (within 0.3 world units); detached glyphs trail the cursor in a fluid arc of magnetic ink; on pointer-stop they snap back to nearest attractor surface and reassemble into a new word drawn from a small embedded vocabulary. Your movement through the field IS the poem. No UI, no instructions — discovery through touch. (C) SEMIOTIC COLLAPSE + REBIRTH — over 90 seconds, glyphs continuously evolve: Latin → Arabic → Devanagari → CJK → geometric primitives (△ ○ □) → pure noise pixels → back to Latin. Each alphabet uses its own atlas texture; a LERP scalar drives the crossfade in the GPGPU shader. The full arc is one 'translation.' Whichever direction chosen: must feel like something a viewer has NEVER SEEN before in browser-native three.js. Ship ONE idea executed at 100%, not three at 30%.

GOOD DIRECTION (differential-growth 3D calligraphic-ink) — but the point geometry is unclear/blurry. Fix sharpness: (1) replace PointsMaterial with CatmullRomCurve3 + TubeGeometry swept along the growth skeleton — this is the preferred ink/vascular technique in this project and gives crisp, readable edge definition. (2) If staying with Points, switch to AlphaTest ≥ 0.5 + hard-edge circle texture (no gaussian falloff), disable sizeAttenuation, reduce point size until each node reads as a distinct mark. (3) No additive blending on the main form — it causes bloom-blur; use NormalBlending with opacity ≥ 0.85. Goal: the calligraphic 'ink' strokes should be LEGIBLE as individual marks, like brushwork, not a smeared fog.

e9c is interesting — keep the line vocabulary. PUSH IT INTO 3D: the lines currently lie in a near-flat plane. Make them genuinely traverse depth — start in the foreground, sweep through to the background, vary z over their length. Use Line2 / LineSegments with explicit z-range = camera frustum-depth × 0.7. The viewer's parallax as the camera orbits should reveal genuine depth, not a flat sheet.

Kusama-obsessive Lucy is a strong concept BUT the per-particle motion currently looks RANDOM / messy. Make the trajectory INTENTFUL — pick ONE coherent flow law per piece: (a) TORNADO — particles spiral around a vertical axis with radius increasing as they rise/fall, (b) RAIN — particles fall along gravity with slight horizontal drift, accumulate or pass through the figure, (c) MAGNETIC FIELD LINES — particles follow visible streamlines emanating from poles, (d) BREATHING TIDE — coordinated inhale-exhale radial expansion/contraction. NEVER independent random walks. The MOTION must read as a single intelligent system, not 60k independent dice rolls.

Klein-blue blot is visually striking but the underlying STRANGE ATTRACTOR base is exhausted as a structural source. Push descendants OFF attractor mathematics into: (a) COSMIC structure — galaxies, accretion disks, nebula filaments, planetary rings, dust lanes; (b) BIOSTRUCTURE — cell walls, viral capsids, protein folds, cytoskeleton, mitotic spindle; (c) SEASHELL / logarithmic-spiral surfaces — nautilus chambers, helicoid shells, mollusc growth lines. KEEP the saturated single-color register, drop the attractor.

DESATURATE THE PALETTE — the composition (kinetic sphere + trace network) is interesting and worth keeping, but every color must be pulled back: max HSL saturation 45%, max lightness 60%. Swap any saturated hue for its dusty/aged counterpart (electric blue → steel-blue-grey, bright orange → rust, vivid green → moss). The spheres should read as old industrial machinery, not neon toys. Keep the trace-accumulation mechanic. No Y-axis rotation.

TWO CHANGES REQUIRED: (1) DESATURATE — same rule as bjk; bring palette to earth-tone restraint (max sat 45%). (2) REPLACE Y-ROTATION WITH LIQUID GALACTIC RIVER FLOW — instead of the structure spinning around Y, the helix/branch form itself should FLOW in a loop, like a galactic arm or a river bending back on itself. The motion is the STRUCTURE moving through space in a closed looping current, not a camera orbiting it. Think: a DNA helix that flows forward like a conveyor belt, or a river of stars spiraling inward. NO camera rotation, NO Y autoRotate. The form moves through itself.

TWO DIRECTIONS TO CHOOSE BETWEEN: (A) GEYSERS — instead of thin expanding lines, have columns of particles SHOOT UPWARD from the calyx base at irregular intervals (like a hot spring or a signal being broadcast from the bowl); the geyser arcs up and falls back, traces hang briefly in the air. High contrast: bright gold/white jets on deep black. (B) BOWL MORPH — the calyx alternates between open-bowl form (wide, shallow) and closed-vessel form (tall, narrow); slow morphing between the two states, like breathing. Pick one and execute it with NO camera rotation. The thin expanding-line mechanic alone is insufficient visual innovation.

SAVE THE BAS-RELIEF SAND SHAKE IDEA — the rail array is dropped (violent random shaking is a hard dislike). But the bas-relief concept is genuinely interesting: (1) Start with particles forming a recognizable IMAGE (a face, a figure, a landscape horizon) as if illuminated from one side — the particles are the 'sand' sitting in the relief grooves. (2) After 8-10 seconds, a gentle vibration causes the sand to FALL OUT of the grooves — particles drift downward under slow gravity. (3) A NEW image assembles from the settling particles (a different face, an abstraction, or a mirror version). The 'shaking' is slow and gravitational, not violent random jitter. Implement as a two-image particle system with lerped target positions + slow y-drift when in 'falling' phase.

FOLDED LEAVES (organic) — user explicitly chose this direction over the earlier Hail Mary brief. User's words: 'i like the folded leaves, be bolder and instead of one piece of leaf, organic combination of different leaf-twirl structures.' Iterations should: (1) DROP the single-stem L-system; build an ARRANGEMENT of multiple folded-leaf elements — like a small bouquet, a fern's mid-uncurling, a clutch of curling autumn leaves caught in a gust, or a spiral of palm-fronds. (2) BE BOLDER — increase the form's footprint to ~40-60% of the frame, exaggerate twirl curvature, layer 5-9 distinct leaf-twirl elements at varying scale and rotation. (3) Each leaf-twirl is a SHEET geometry (PlaneGeometry / curved BufferGeometry strip), not a tree skeleton. Use a calligraphic mid-vein + curling edge — fern-uncurling, palm-frond, or autumn-leaf-twist vocabulary. (4) BUG TO REMOVE: the current piece has a barbell/dumbbell render artifact at the end of the structure — two pale dots connected by a vertical line. Eliminate it. (5) Palette stays warm-amber on near-black; restraint in motion.
